citations.long: Procedures describing the warehousing of drug products are not established.
Aseptic processing areas are deficient regarding the system for monitoring environmental conditions.
Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of drug products is not of appropriate design, of adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use.
Procedures designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile are not written.
Drug products are not stored under appropriate conditions of temperature so that their identity, strength, quality, and purity are not affected.

citations.short: Computer control of master formula records
citations.long: Appropriate controls are not exercised over computers or related systems to assure that changes in master production and control records or other records are instituted only by authorized personnel.

citations.short: Adequate number of batches on stability
citations.long: An adequate number of batches of each drug product are not tested nor are records of such data maintained to determine an appropriate expiration date.

citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.

citations.short: Control procedures to monitor and validate performance
citations.long: Control procedures are not established which monitor the output and validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.
Written procedures are not established that describe the in-process controls and tests to be conducted on appropriate samples of in-process materials of each batch.
Procedures designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile are not written.
Labels and other labeling materials are not stored separately with suitable identification for each different drug product, strength, dosage form or quantity of contents.
Written records of investigations into the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and follow-up.
